name: BAC 167 Strikemaster / Jet Provost
summary: British side-by-side jet trainer, the RAF's basic jet trainer for decades, with the armed Strikemaster variant exported to several air forces; many ex-RAF examples fly in the US as warbirds.

wings: Low, straight wing with a thin section
engines: Single Viper turbojet with wing-root intakes on each side
fuselage: Side-by-side seating under a large, rounded bubble canopy
Retractable tricycle gear on short legs
tail: Straight fin with a small dorsal fillet
Horizontal tail mounted mid-way on the fuselage

tellTales: Side-by-side seats under a big bubble canopy on a small straight-wing jet
Wing-root intakes and tip tanks on a stubby jet
Short legs and a stubby, rounded nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The L-29 has tandem canopies and a pot-belly; the Jet Provost has side-by-side seats under one big canopy.
The Magister has a V-tail and tandem seats; the Jet Provost has a conventional tail and side-by-side seats.
The S-211 has a shoulder wing and tandem seats; the Jet Provost has a low wing and side-by-side seats.
The T-33 has tandem seats and a long slim nose; the Jet Provost has side-by-side seats and a stubby nose.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
